newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, April 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, April 14.

text.p: The following are the highlights of stories from the Irish press on Monday.

- The gloves were off on Sunday as the main opposition party Fianna Fail and Ireland's Labour Party, one of the three coalition parties in government, engaged in bitter clashes after Dick Spring, leader of the Labour Party, drew the battle lines for the election campaign.
- A 14-year-old boy and a 23-year-old male have been charged with the manslaughter of an Irishman in Manchester.
- The Irish Central Bank's prayers for a showdown in borrowing may be answered, according to a new survey.

- The battle lines are drawn for an aggressive election campaign next month following the categorical decision by Dick Spring, leader of Ireland's Labour Party, to rule out a coalition between his party and the main opposition party Fianna Fail in the event of a hung parliament.
- Eight Catholic families were forced out of their homes by a loyalist mob on Saturday night in the Limestone Road area of Belfast.
- EU Agriculture Commissioner, Franz Fischler, has ruled out any direct aid to the Irish beef industry. - An Irish compromise on fishery cuts, involving fleet cuts and
reduced catching effort, is to be debated at the EU fisheries council in Luxembourg on Monday.
- Ireland's Progressive Democrats party on Sunday greeted with delight the decision by Labour Party leader, Dick Spring, to firmly rule out coalition with the main opposition party Fianna Fail.
- Avonmore have offered Waterford Foods a mere one-third stake in the 2.5 billion Irish pounds super-company which would be created from their proposed merger.
